summary: The note describes how quantum computing threatens public-key cryptography such as RSA and ECC, and how industry, governments and researchers are responding from September 2023 onward. It covers a key experiment, lattice-based encryption, collaborative alliances, workforce education, legislation and regulation, monitoring startups, and Quantum Key Distribution. It ends on an optimistic view that the challenge will drive stronger, more resilient security.
one_line: Overview of the quantum hacking threat to encryption and the technical, educational, regulatory and collaborative responses emerging since September 2023.
key_facts: Dr. Linda Chen, a quantum physicist at the California Quantum Institute, said on September 3, 2023 that "Quantum computers can, in theory, break many of the cryptographic systems currently in place."

On September 15, 2023, a team led by Dr. Amir Khasrowshahi at QuantumTech Laboratories showed that a sufficiently powerful quantum computer could break a commonly used encryption algorithm in just hours, a task that would take a conventional supercomputer thousands of years.
The experiment showed quantum computers could realistically threaten encryption methods like RSA and ECC.
Public-key cryptography, which secures everything from emails to financial transactions, is the most talked-about target of quantum computers.
On September 25, 2023, Dr. Emily Jackson announced that her team at SecureQuant Technologies had deployed a lattice-based encryption protocol tested to be robust against quantum attacks.
Lattice-based cryptography relies on the mathematical complexity of lattice problems that even quantum computers find hard to solve.
The International Quantum Safe Alliance was established on October 15 to create standards and best practices and to enable knowledge sharing among stakeholders.
Dr. Raj Singh said on October 7, 2023 that migration to quantum-resistant algorithms must include hardware manufacturers, software developers, cybersecurity professionals, and users.
Jacqueline Santos, a cybersecurity trainer, hosted a webinar series starting October 21 on identifying and protecting against quantum vulnerabilities.

In November 2023 the US government passed legislation funding the Quantum Cybersecurity Preparedness Act, mandating federal agencies to inventory their systems and upgrade to quantum-resistant cryptography.
The European Union's Cybersecurity Agency published regulations on November 20 requiring member states to audit their security systems and comply with quantum-resistant standards by 2025.
Quantum Sentinel, a startup launched in December 2023, offers quantum threat detection and real-time AI-based monitoring.
Quantum Secure Communications began deploying Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) in critical infrastructure in early 2024; QKD faces challenges of high costs and specialized hardware.
